messages:
Lina Park: FYI customer Acme reported a sudden flood of 401s on our /callbacks endpoint after they rotated IdP keys. They say they started signing with new kid 'k-new' at 2026-03-15T15:01Z and we started rejecting at ~15:03Z. Ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/ACME-4721
AJ: Paste of edge verification output? Any 'kid not found' lines?
Lina Park: Edge log snippet:
```
verify_jwt: KidLookupError: kid not found (kid=\"k-new\") jwks_etag=\"W/\\\"etag-77\\\"\" cache_status=304 tenant=acme-prod endpoint=/callbacks/webhook trace=tx-9f2b
```
Lina Park: They also mentioned a clock jump on some machines; a batch of tokens had iat about 75-95s ahead of our clock.
AJ: That cache_status=304 plus kid-not-found is suspicious. Looks like our JWKS client did an If-None-Match, got 304, and kept the old key set which doesn't include k-new. If the IdP returned 304 incorrectly during rotation (or CDN cached stale 304), we'd miss the rotated key.
Tom (oncall): Confirmed spike from Acme IPs at 2026-03-15T15:03:xxZ. Our JWKS TTL is 10m + conditional fetch; this exact scenario can cause short-lived outages during partner rotations.
Kevin M.: Quick mitigations we can do now:
- Force clear the tenant JWKS cache (ops)
- Ask Acme to pause or revert rotation for ~10m if possible
- Temporarily increase JWT leeway for that tenant (e.g., +120s) to account for clock drift
AJ: Repro steps for infra/devs to simulate the broken conditional GET:
1) Simulate idp responding with 304 to If-None-Match:
```
curl -i -H "If-None-Match: W/\"etag-77\"" https://idp.acme.com/.well-known/jwks.json
# HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified
# (empty body)
```
2) Post a token signed with the freshly rotated kid k-new to our callback endpoint. Observe 401 and log showing kid-not-found.
Expected: Our jwks client should, on kid-miss + fetch_status=304, attempt one forced full-fetch (ignore 304) before giving up.
Tom (oncall): I cleared the acme-prod JWKS cache just now. Monitoring shows 401s dropped to near 0 within ~40s.
Lina Park: Thanks. Customer confirmed callback calls succeed again. I'll add a ticket note: temporary cache clear + asked them to hold rotation for 10m.
AJ: I'll prepare a small code patch to add a force-fetch-on-kid-miss path and a DEFAULT_JWT_LEEWAY env var (120s). Pseudo: 
```
if (!jwks.find(kid)) {
  if (last_fetch_status == 304 && !tried_force_fetch) {
    jwks.force_fetch(ignore_cache=true);
    tried_force_fetch = true;
    // retry find(kid)
  }
}
// validate iat/exp with configurable leeway
```
Kevin M.: Also add metrics and alerts: jwks.force_fetch_count and jwks.kid_missing_rate; alert if kid_missing_rate > 5% for a tenant over 5m.
Lina Park: For postmortem/actions: add a runbook entry for this symptom (kid-miss + 304 + partner rotation) with steps: clear cache, ask partner to pause, enable leeway if needed, and deploy permanent fix.
support-bot: inc-3023456790 created: "Acme jwt verification spike" assigned to eng-security :rotating_light:
AJ: I'll open PR with tests that simulate 304 then changed JWKS body and assert force_fetch occurs. Will stage, soak 30m, then roll to prod. PR link (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/jwks-client/pull/790
Lina Park: Good work. Keep this thread for follow-ups; I'll update the ticket and close once PR is live and Acme confirms.
Kevin M.: I'll add a short pager rule for sustained kid-mismatch spikes and add runbook blurb.
Lina Park: Resolved for now. Leaving the thread for next steps and docs.
